question: At batch 8 and active NGRAM depth 6, does the source-complete exact CUDA graph preserve the full producer-to-consumer contract and reduce component latency versus identical eager execution on H100?

bench.availability_gate: Do not inspect, claim, or mutate the bench while priority-8500 owns it. After that project releases, read its current identity from runtime/gpus.json and claim it once if available.
bench.reuse: Preserve all resident checkpoint, image, source, workload, and cache state. This component loads no checkpoint and may add at most 2 GiB of source, build cache, and result artifacts.

component.alternation: Alternate the two arms with deterministic inputs after warmup.
component.trace: Capture one short trace spanning both arms and one 7-to-8-to-7 graph-key transition guard.

require: identical accepted token IDs and lengths
identical KV destinations and scheduler offsets
exact graph key includes speculative depth
no stale mask or buffer tail is consumed
7-to-8-to-7 transition remains fail-closed against key aliasing
correctness.numerical_gate: Record the maximum target-attention absolute error and require it to match the established component tolerance.
correctness.failure: Any ownership, key, token, KV, or settlement mismatch is a component negative; do not infer endpoint performance.

telemetry: CUDA-event latency for each complete arm

budgets.compute: At most one retained H100 claim after priority-8500 releases it.
